instructions.purpose: Schedule recurring events that fire automatically at defined intervals using cron patterns. Use this tool when the user wants to set up a reminder, periodic notification, or any task that should repeat on a regular schedule.

tool.name: schedule-recurring
tool.description: Creates a recurring cron job identified by a unique name that fires at intervals defined by a 5-field cron expression. Also stores either direct reminder text or wording-only regeneration data, or an autonomous web task with fallback text. Returns the scheduled job details including the next fire time.

instructions.cron_patterns:
Use standard 5-field cron expressions: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week
Common examples: - "0 9 * * *" — every day at 9:00 - "*/30 * * * *" — every 30 minutes - "0 8 * * 1" — every Monday at 8:00 - "0 0 1 * *" — first of every month at midnight - "0 9 * * 1-5" — weekdays at 9:00

usage_rules.rule: After this tool succeeds, return the schedule and reminder or autonomous objective to Main
Choose clear, descriptive names for jobs so they can be easily referenced later
If a job with the same name already exists, set overwrite to true only if the user explicitly agrees to replace it
Validate that the cron pattern matches the user's intended schedule before calling
Provide exactly one mode: reminderText; reminderPromptData plus reminderFallbackText; or taskPrompt plus taskFallbackText
Use taskPrompt when firing-time web search or fetch is required; use reminderPromptData only for fresh wording that needs no tools
Pass reminderPromptData as a serialized JSON string, not as a nested object
Include the next fire time in the result returned to Main

example.context: User says: "Every morning at 8, send me a briefing on the latest AI news"

toolCall.name: daily-ai-news
toolCall.taskPrompt: Find the most important AI news published since the previous morning. Summarize it with direct source links.
toolCall.taskFallbackText: I could not prepare today's AI news briefing.

example.reasoning: The answer depends on fresh web information at firing time, so use scheduled-task mode.
